propertyNames.$comment: A namespace Prefix is an XML NCName [NAMESPACES], not an ACAL IdentifierType (no {ShortId} macro-substitution). The normative lexical space is the full NCName production - see acal-xpath-v1.0.md Section 5.2 - which includes non-ASCII name characters. This pattern is an ASCII-only approximation: a portable JSON Schema 'pattern' cannot express the full NCName character ranges. It is a validation floor, not a narrowing - an instance whose prefix is a valid non-ASCII NCName is conformant per Section 5.2 even though it will not match here. 'xmlns' is never permitted as a prefix by [NAMESPACES]; 'xml' is permitted only when bound to its own fixed URI, and Section 5.2 already treats that binding as implicitly available in every representation - so neither is a useful key here and both are excluded. The empty string key is the separate, valid default-namespace declaration.

NamespaceDeclarationsType.$comment: Maps each namespace Prefix (the empty string denotes the default namespace) directly to its Name (URI), rather than an array of {Prefix, Name} pair-objects, per issue #134. A producer SHALL NOT emit a duplicate key; a consumer SHALL reject one. JSON Schema cannot enforce this, since a validator only sees the instance after parsing, by which point a duplicate key has already been resolved in an implementation-defined way (RFC 8259) - see acal-xpath-v1.0.md Section 5.2 for the normative producer/consumer requirement.

allOf.$comment: Namespaces is OPTIONAL (issue #134): absent (equivalently empty) means the Path expression needs no supplied namespace-prefix bindings - all its names resolve without one, or it matches namespaces via wildcards / namespace-uri() / URIQualifiedNames. There is no Defaults-level namespace table to fall back on - see acal-xpath-v1.0.md Section 5.3.3.
Namespaces is OPTIONAL (issue #134): absent means the Path expression needs no namespace-prefix bindings. Same rule as XPathAttributeSelectorType - see acal-xpath-v1.0.md Section 5.3.4.

XPathExpressionValueType.$comment: XPathVersion and Namespaces are both OPTIONAL here (issue #134). XPathVersion: in a Request or Policy, a value with no local XPathVersion takes it from the applicable XPathRequestDefaults / XPathPolicyDefaults; a value in a response, or with no applicable Defaults in scope, MUST carry XPathVersion locally - that contextual requirement cannot be expressed in JSON Schema. Namespaces: absent means the XPath expression needs no namespace-prefix bindings; there is no Defaults-level namespace table to fall back on. See acal-xpath-v1.0.md Section 5.3.5.
